item.title: Ryan Specialty launches Tera Underwriters
item.description: Ryan Specialty Underwriting Managers has launched Tera Underwriters , a managing general underwriter focused on industrial-scale computing hardware used in cryptocurrency mining and AI and high-performance computing data centers. The program is available in all 50 states exclusively through RT Specialty, with international capabilities expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. The Lloyd’s-backed program covers ASICs, GPUs, networking infrastructure and related equipment.

item.title: Severe Thunderstorms Across US Midwest Trigger Flood Warnings
item.description: Midwest and Ohio Valley, including Chicago and Cincinnati, face an enhanced, or level 3, risk of severe thunderstorms. New York City is forecast to have a high of 88F (31C) with a 30% chance of showers and thunderstorms after 2 p.m.

item.title: FAA Orders Crack Inspections for Certain Boeing 737 Max Jets
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration this week ordered inspections for hundreds of Boeing planes, following reports of cracks in some older models. 10, applies to certain aircraft under three Boeing 737 Max models: the 737-8, 737-9 and 737-8200. The Max jets have “a similar design and build process” to the older models, “making those airplanes susceptible to the same crack condition,” the FAA wrote in November.

item.title: U.S. Court Rules Meta, Other Tech Firms Must Face Lawsuits Over Social Media Addiction
item.description: appeals court on Monday allowed thousands of lawsuits to move forward against Meta Platforms, Alphabet’s Google, ByteDance’s TikTok and Snap Inc’s Snapchat over claims they designed their products to be addictive to young users. Circuit Court of Appeals rejected an appeal by Meta and TikTok seeking to overturn a lower court ruling requiring them to face more than 3,000 lawsuits filed in federal court, saying the companies had appealed too early. META LOSES BID TO DELAY MULTI-STATE TRIAL The court also denied Meta’s bid to postpone a trial beginning on Wednesday in a lawsuit brought by 29 state attorneys general alleging that the company illegally collected and used children’s data, designed its social media platforms to keep young users hooked, and misled consumers about their safety.

item.title: Rising Seas Not the Only Threat to Coastal Cities
item.description: A new study highlights the two fold threat coastal cities face: rising seas and sinking land. The main reason for the difference is land subsidence, the gradual sinking of the ground beneath coastal cities and communities. Researchers from the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and Tulane University found that this downward movement of land is greatly increasing the amount of sea level rise experienced by millions of coastal residents.

item.title: Vantage Partnership Capital (AdVantage) generated $23m of fee income in Q2 2026
item.description: The third-party reinsurance capital platform of Bermuda headquartered re/insurer Vantage Risk, recently acquired by the Bill Ackman linked Howard Hughes Holdings, generated $23 million of fee income from its insurance-linked securities style partnerships with investors in the second-quarter of 2026. It’s the first visibility of the profitability of the Vantage Partnership Capital operation, which undertakes its business through the AdVantage platform of companies. When Howard Hughes Holdings announced its acquisition of Vantage Risk, its senior executives explained that AdVantage and the Vantage Partnership Capital business is seen as an attractive “high-margin, asset-light fee stream.” Bill Ackman himself stated on AdVantage that it is appealing because it is “an asset management business, you have third-party capital, and you get a management fee and a piece of the upside.” Ackman further said, “That’s a very high ROE business, and that’s a business that today has about a billion and a half of third party capital.

item.title: AI to drive catastrophe bond expansion, including into data centre risks: Ethan Powell, Brookmont
item.description: As the insurance-linked securities (ILS) and catastrophe bond markets continue to embrace artificial intelligence (AI), the technology has the potential to help expand the market into new sectors like data centre risks, according to Ethan Powell, Principal and CIO of Brookmont Capital Management. “And the sponsors themselves are better able to more quickly assimilate data and more accurately structure deals and have better attachment points with better pricing, which means they’re able to support those deal terms and deal structures better with more contemporaneous data.” A key area that AI is being implemented across the industry is through catastrophe models, in which Powell believes is ultimately helping to improve deal structures and terms across the cat bond market. To begin, Powell emphasised how AI has advanced so heavily over the last year, and how this is impacting the catastrophe bond market.

item.title: Severe weather drives insured losses past $840m in Manitoba and Saskatchewan: CatIQ
item.description: Severe weather losses in Manitoba and Saskatchewan – neighbouring provinces located in Western and Central Canada – have climbed above $840 million, according to the latest estimate from Catastrophe Indices and Quantification Inc. Since 2021, Manitoba and Saskatchewan have experienced 30 catastrophic weather events resulting in over $2.5 billion in insured losses. So far in 2026, five of Canada’s 11 catastrophic weather events have affected Manitoba and Saskatchewan, including a dust storm with damaging winds that caused $40 million in insured losses.

Simeone will report to incoming US CEO Nadine Moore and Group Chief Risk Officer Sheldon Lacy. Her appointment also deepens the global collaboration between our risk teams, ensuring the US benefits from our Group-wide expertise – and the Group benefits from hers.” Simeone added: “I am excited to be joining Canopius at such an important point in its growth journey in the US.

item.title: Aon’s NFP acquires Frontier Risk’s retail cannabis business
item.description: NFP, an Aon company and property and casualty (P&C) broker and benefits consultant, has announced the acquisition of the retail cannabis business of Frontier Risk Group, Inc. Together, we’ll offer clients deeper industry insight, more specialized risk management guidance and access to the broad resources of NFP’s national platform.” According to the announcement, Frontier Risk Group will focus on scaling Strata Specialty, its multi-program manager, following the sale of its retail cannabis business. “Frontier Risk’s cannabis business is a natural fit for our Life Sciences practice,” said Foster.

item.title: Delta-8 Among Products Banned as Texas THC Suit Continues
item.description: State officials banned at the end of last month several hemp-derived THC cannabis products, including those containing delta-8 and delta-10 THC variants, with possible punishment including jail time and fines. A federal judge denied an emergency motion for a temporary restraining order sought by hemp businesses and consumers, allowing the Texas ban on THC products to continue until the case is resolved. However, delta-9 THC, the most commonly sold THC product in Texas, will remain legal.

item.title: Officials Urge Gulf Coast Beachgoers to Beware of Deadly Bacterial Infections
item.description: Health officials in Louisiana are urging beachgoers to take precautions during a summertime surge in infections from a flesh-eating bacteria found in coastal waters. Most infections are reported from May to October, and most happen in states along the Gulf Coast. Louisiana has confirmed nine cases of Vibrio vulnificus infections this year, the state’s health department said last week in a news release .

item.title: Florida’s Mangrove Insurance Launches Sidecar Reinsurance Vehicle
item.description: Petersburg-based Mangrove Property Insurance, launched two years ago, has created its own reinsurance sidecar, the company announced. Mangrove was granted a certificate of authority by the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation in January 2025. “Our successful launch of Grove Re reflects Mangrove’s commitment to invest in both capabilities and financial protection to fulfil our mission of being a partner for the long-term with policyholders and agents across Florida.” A Class 3A reinsurer must have a percentage of unrelated business that represents 50% or more of net premiums written or net loss and loss expense provisions, and where the unrelated business net premiums are less than $50 million, according to the Bermuda Monetary Authority.

item.title: DogPack partners with Healthy Paws
item.description: DogPack, a platform connecting dog owners through discovery, social content, and marketplace experiences, announced a partnership with Healthy Paws. “Healthy Paws has always believed that every pet deserves the best possible care, and that starts with making great coverage accessible. Together, we’re making it easier than ever for families to protect the pets that matter most to them.” – Alex Faynberg, EVP of Healthy Paws.

item.title: MetLife Pet partners with America’s VetDogs
item.description: MetLife Pet Insurance has partnered with America’s VetDogs to sponsor the training and development of a service dog for a veteran or first responder with a disability. Through America’s VetDogs’ Puppy with a Purpose program, Charlie will spend approximately 14 to 18 months with a volunteer puppy raiser in the New York Tri-State Area before beginning advanced training and being matched with a handler. America’s VetDogs provides trained service dogs to veterans, first responders and active-duty service members at no cost.

item.title: YuLife reports latest financial results
item.description: Life insurance startup YuLife has released its financial results for the year ended June 30, 2025. YuLife operates in the UK, US, South Africa, and Japan, but less than 2% of revenue was generated outside the UK. Revenue grew 40% YoY to £13.9M, driven mainly by SaaS income (£3.8M), while group risk products revenue stayed flat at £7.2M.

item.title: Update: Colombia Suffers Widespread Damage From Magnitude 7.4 Quake
item.description: The magnitude 7.4 quake struck at 7:34 a.m. A deadly earthquake hit Colombia on Monday morning, toppling buildings, burying people under rubble and leaving more than 100 dead in the Pacific region and the central Andes. Significant damage was reported in the country’s coffee heartland, the region immediately east of the epicenter.

item.title: Connected Vendor Networks Modernize Insurance Claim Payouts
item.description: That gap between payment approval and claim resolution is spurring the rise of vendor provider networks in insurance. Vendor networks let insurers reuse validated payment instructions instead of rebuilding the same vendor relationships claim by claim. The networks connect carriers with the businesses they pay during a claim, preserve vendor payment preferences and reduce the need for every insurer to establish the same relationships separately.

item.title: Global insured cat losses reach $42bn in H1 2026, lowest first-half since 2020: Swiss Re
item.description: The Swiss Re Institute has estimated that global insured losses from natural catastrophe events reached US $42 billion in the first half of 2026, marking the lowest first-half total recorded since 2020, and 16% below the 10-year average. In addition, Swiss Re estimated that global economic losses from nat cat events reached $100 billion in the first half of 2026, considerably down from H1 2025’s $152 billion and 10% below the 10-year average. Swiss Re’s data on global insured natural catastrophe losses of $42 billion for H1 2026 compares to broker Aon’s estimate of at least $47 billion, and reinsurance broker Gallagher Re’s estimate of at least $46 billion.

item.title: Progressive renews $2.19bn of CAT XoL reinsurance for Florida, $1.85bn for other states
item.description: US insurer Progressive has renewed its per-occurrence property catastrophe excess-of-loss reinsurance program to provide it with $2.19 billion of limits for first events affecting Florida and $1.85 billion of coverage for first events impacting other states, at the June 1 renewals. At the June 1 reinsurance renewals, Progressive has renewed its property per-occurrence excess of loss (XoL) tower, which with the additional coverage from catastrophe bonds and its Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund (FHCF) participation, now provides $2.19 billion for a first event in Florida and $1.85 billion for a first event outside of Florida, also including the shared limit protection purchased at the start of this year. It’s a similar sized reinsurance tower to the Progressive renewal at the mid-year of 2025 at around $2.2 billion , while this year the company has $400 million of outstanding Bonanza Re catastrophe bond protection as part of its 2026 reinsurance arrangements.

item.title: Specialty MGA hires Simon Woodage to build NA Property Treaty portfolio
item.description: Specialty MGA, the managing general agent within MNK Group, has appointed experienced reinsurance professional Simon Woodage as Senior Underwriter for North American Property Treaty, as it expands its presence in the treaty reinsurance market. Woodage’s appointment will see him take responsibility for developing Specialty MGA’s North American Property Treaty business, with a focus on establishing the portfolio, setting its underwriting approach and building relationships with insurers and brokers across the sector. While modelling remains an important tool, underwriting judgement and strong relationships will continue to be central to our approach.” The appointment forms part of Specialty MGA’s wider development of its treaty reinsurance offering, with Woodage expected to lead the North American Property Treaty operation as the portfolio is established.

item.title: Traditional reinsurers face test of discipline as casualty risk remains hard to price: AM Best
item.description: AM Best, the global credit rating agency, says casualty reinsurance is becoming a growing strategic concern for traditional reinsurers as record levels of capital meet uncertainty over long-term loss trends. In its report, Global Reinsurance at an Inflection Point: Can Discipline Survive the Temptation of Record Capital?, AM Best notes that casualty reinsurance presents a different challenge from property catastrophe business because the market is harder to classify as either hard or soft. For AM Best, one of the key questions for casualty reinsurers is whether recent rate increases are keeping pace with underlying loss costs.

item.title: Typhoon Season Forecast to Be Among Most Intense Ever for Asia
item.description: The current typhoon season in the Northwest Pacific Ocean is shaping up to be one of the most intense on record as the El Niño system strengthens, according to the latest projection by commercial forecaster Tropical Storm Risk. Read more : Typhoon Season in Northwest Pacific Seen Most Active in a Decade “A strong El Niño event has developed and is forecast to intensify further through the rest of summer and autumn,” Adam Lea, manager at Tropical Storm Risk, wrote in the report, adding that this would have “a strong enhancing effect” on the typhoon season. Asia’s typhoon season typically runs from June to October, though the destructive storms can also form in other months.

item.title: Houthi Attack on Small Cargo Ship in Red Sea Kills Three Crew Members, Sources Say
item.description: A small cargo ship was attacked by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis in the Bab el-Mandeb strait on Tuesday, killing three crew members, said two Yemeni coast guard sources and two military officials in the government. British maritime security company Ambrey said the ship was reportedly targeted and damaged by the Houthis, killing three crew members, while at anchor 3.3 nautical miles northeast of Perim Island, Yemen. After the attack, the crew lost control of the ship and were approached by Yemeni coast guard, they added.

item.title: Marsh McLennan Agency to acquire Accel Holdings
item.description: Marsh McLennan Agency (MMA) has agreed to acquire Accel Holdings, a diversified independent insurance and advisory firm based in Waverly, Iowa. Founded in 1936, Accel provides commercial and personal insurance, employee benefits and agribusiness solutions, alongside wealth management and retirement advisory services. The firm expanded through a 2018 merger with Millhiser Smith Agency, which was founded in 1928.

item.title: Allstate develops Allie platform for agentic AI strategy
item.description: Allstate is developing a proprietary agentic AI platform called Allie as the insurer looks to embed AI more deeply across its operations and customer interactions. CEO Tom Wilson outlined the initiative during Allstate’s second-quarter earnings call, saying the platform is intended to support the company’s broader technology-driven strategy. Allstate has not provided a timeline for Allie’s launch.

item.title: EverQuote takes minority stake in Waniwani
item.description: EverQuote has entered into an exclusive commercial partnership with Waniwani and made a strategic minority investment in the company. EverQuote plans to integrate Waniwani’s technology into its AI solutions for P&C carriers and insurance agents. By developing new products and integrating technologies like Waniwani, we will extend our portfolio of growth solutions for P&C carriers and agents and give our customers the tools they need to stay visible and competitive in this new landscape, not just for today’s digital channels, but for the agentic AI channels that are quickly becoming just as important.” – Jayme Mendal, CEO of EverQuote.

item.title: How AI is Changing Insurance Reconciliation Workflows
item.description: Reconciliation is one of the most critical and time-consuming financial workflows for insurance organizations. The Reconciliation Agent is designed specifically for insurance accounting workflows to help organizations automatically align carrier statements with agency transactions and support revenue, commissions, and payables processes with greater accuracy and efficiency. The next evolution of insurance workflows The Reconciliation Agent demonstrates how AI can enhance complex insurance workflows when it is built with industry-specific needs in mind.

item.title: Trump Wins Permission to Revise BBC Suit to Remove Brand Damage
item.description: Trump’s suit alleged that the clip, which didn’t air in the US, resulted in “massive economic damage to his brand value and significant damage and injury to his future financial prospects, in addition to continuing to harm his reputation as President of the United States of America.” In response, lawyers for the BBC issued sweeping subpoenas to the Trump Organization demanding financial records spanning a period of time from before and after the documentary aired. President Donald Trump won court permission to revise his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the British Broadcasting Corp. A magistrate judge upheld the subpoenas at a hearing in July, even after Trump’s lawyer said he would seek to amend the suit to focus only on alleged damage to Trump’s reputation.

item.title: Climate-driven SCS to reshape how insurers price risk: First Street
item.description: Severe convective storms (hail, damaging wind, and tornadoes) have become the costliest insured peril of the 21st century, reshaping how insurers, investors, and asset owners price risk, new First Street analysis reveals. New research released by First Street, titled Global Severe Convective Storm Risk: Pricing Economic Exposure to a Rising Peril, provides the first globally consistent analysis mapping out where SCS hazards collide with dense populations and economic assets, alongside an analysis of how rapidly this exposure is expanding. Severe convective storms have become one of the fastest-growing sources of physical climate risk.

item.title: Appeals Court Says Lobstermen’s Defamation Suit Raises First Amendment Questions
item.description: One of the appellate judges, Judge Seth Aframe, said during oral arguments on July 27 that it doesn’t strike him as a defamation claim and that he finds the case troubling “from a First Amendment perspective.” “The more you broaden the class of people that fall within this, the more it feels like everybody can sue,” Aframe said. A federal appeals court signaled that it might not allow a lawsuit brought by fishing industry businesses and trade groups against a California aquarium to proceed because of the case’s potential impact on free speech. Circuit Court of Appeals is deciding whether the lawsuit can go forward.

item.title: Appeal Court: Social Media Companies Must Face Thousands of Addiction Lawsuits
item.description: appeals court on Monday allowed thousands of lawsuits to move forward against Meta Platforms, Alphabet’s Google, ByteDance’s TikTok, and other social media companies over claims they designed their products to be addictive to young users. Circuit Court of Appeals rejected the companies’ bid to reverse a lower court’s ruling forcing them to face more than 3,000 lawsuits over the claims filed in federal court, concluding that the appeal came too early in the litigation. Filed by states, municipalities, school districts and individuals, the lawsuits allege that social media companies intentionally addicted young users, contributing to surging depression, anxiety and body-image issues and a broader mental health crisis among American youth in recent years.
